hints: Focus on the oxidation number of chlorine in each reaction, and ask whether it goes up, goes down, or stays the same.
Remember that $\text{Cl}^-$ from $\text{NaCl}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ simply forms $\text{HCl}$ gas with no change in oxidation state, unlike $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$.
Check if $\text{Cl}_2$ in water and in cold $\text{NaOH}$ both split into two different oxidation states while also producing acids.
walkthrough:
**Test statement 1 - conc. acid with NaCl**

Think acid-base first, not redox. Chloride is a weak reducing agent and is not oxidised by concentrated sulfuric acid.

$$\text{NaCl(s) + H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(l) } \rightarrow \text{ NaHSO}_4\text{(s) + HCl(g)}$$

**Check oxidation numbers in statement 1**

In $\text{Cl}^-$ the oxidation number is $-1$, and in $\text{HCl}$ it is still $-1$. No electron loss, so no oxidation. Statement 1 is incorrect.

**Test statement 2 - chlorine with cold NaOH**

This is the classic bleach reaction. The same element, $\text{Cl}_2$ at $0$, is both reduced and oxidised.

$$\text{Cl}_2\text{(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) } \rightarrow \text{ NaCl(aq) + NaClO(aq) + H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

**Confirm disproportionation and test statement 3**

Here $\text{Cl}(0) \rightarrow \text{Cl}(-1)$ in $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{Cl}(0) \rightarrow \text{Cl}(+1)$ in $\text{NaClO}$. That is disproportionation, so statement 2 is correct.

For water: $$\text{Cl}_2\text{(aq) + H}_2\text{O(l) } \rightleftharpoons \text{ HCl(aq) + HClO(aq)}$$

**Conclude which statements are correct**

Both $\text{HCl}$, a strong acid, and $\text{HClO}$, a weak acid, make the solution acidic. So statement 3 is correct.

Only 2 and 3 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, but 1 is wrong because $\text{Cl}^-$ is not oxidised to $\text{Cl}_2$, it only forms $\text{HCl}$.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is false. Students choose this if they confuse $\text{Cl}^-$ with $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$, which are oxidised by concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
options.C: Correct. Statement 2 is a disproportionation ($0$ to $-1$ and $+1$) and statement 3 produces acidic $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HClO}$. Statement 1 is false, so 2 and 3 only is the right combination.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims only statement 1 is correct. In fact statement 1 is the only false statement, as oxidation number of Cl stays at $-1$ when $\text{HCl}$ forms.
